objective.statement: Authorise or deny a deploy transport for the live harness, on proof that the transport was exercised on a control file AND that rollback was executed once for real.
objective.charter: MANDATE. Choosing a deploy transport is a critical, hard-to-reverse decision, so the council votes as a logical AND: every seat must consent, and any single seat withholding consent denies. Two proofs are required. (1) The transport must be proven on a CONTROL file - a file whose before and after bytes you know - because a deploy tool that reports exit 0 while copying nothing looks identical to a successful one. An exit-0 with count=0 is fail-open success, not a deploy. (2) Rollback must be EXECUTED once, not merely documented; a rollback path that has never run is a plan, not a capability. Banned transports stay banned: the known-bad path is a --deploy mode that mutates the live tree, and its read-only --check sibling is the only safe form.
success_criteria: the transport moved a known control file, verified byte-for-byte at the destination
rollback was executed once and the tree returned to its prior state
an exit-0 / count-0 result is classified as FAIL, not as success
every banned transport is named and shown unused

forbidden_actions: run a deploy mode that mutates the live tree during evaluation
accept an exit-0 with a zero-file count as a successful deploy
authorise a transport whose rollback has never been executed

roster.display_name: SRE - owns the live tree and the rollback

context.briefing: Run the control-file proof yourself. The destination bytes are the verdict; the tool's exit code is a hint. Verify the rollback by executing it, then confirm the tree matches its pre-deploy state.

roster.display_name: Security - transport trust and blast radius
Owner representative - carries the owner's standing constraints

committees.mandate: Exercise the candidate transport on a known control file and verify destination bytes independently of the tool's exit code.
Execute rollback once for real and confirm the tree returns to its pre-deploy state.

sequence.custom_name: deploy a known control file and verify destination bytes
execute rollback once and verify restoration

stopping.source_expression: custom:transport_proven_on_control_file == true AND custom:rollback_executed_once == true AND NOT custom:fail_open_exit_zero_count_zero == true

conditional_decision_requires: the transport is re-proven on a control file in the target environment

owner_approval_for: any write to the live harness tree

metadata.title: Harness deploy-transport gate (binding, critical)
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: C-H53 `harness-deploy-transport-gate`, global ordinal 53, tier standard, protocols P18/P51, 4 seats, 2 rounds, default binding BINDING, risk critical, OWNER-DECISION YES. || EDITABLE DIALS: (1) banned_transports -> objective.owner_constraints.forbidden_actions plus the control-file-proof stage; name the specific transport modes that may not be exercised at all. Secondary dials: budgets.time_minutes (30), voting.veto.holders, protocol.experiments.runner (sandbox by default so an evaluation cannot touch the live tree), consensus.threshold (1 = unanimity). || VOCABULARY MAP (design term -> CouncilSpec enum): voting `logical_AND` -> voting.method `unanimity` with quorum.min_fraction 1 and consensus.threshold 1; every seat must consent and one hold-out denies. Additionally three seats hold an explicit veto so a denial is attributable rather than emergent. roles `sre` -> custom:sre, `security` -> security_reviewer (enum), `implementer` -> custom:implementer, `owner_rep` -> custom:owner_rep with kind `human`, vendor `human` and authority `owner`. Outcome names map AUTHORISE -> decision, DENY -> no_decision, CONDITIONAL_DECISION -> conditional_decision; the schema has no AUTHORISE/DENY tokens, so a denial is structurally a `no_decision` (nothing is authorised) and the reason lives in the dissent record. `default binding: binding` has no field: it is encoded as outcomes.allowed containing `decision`, and the owner countersignature is objective.owner_constraints.approval_required true. `evidence standard: executable_receipt` -> anchor_style `command_output` plus outputs.receipt_schema. || CUSTOM METRICS AND THEIR PRODUCERS: custom:transport_proven_on_control_file (boolean; produced by the control-file-proof stage comparing destination bytes, NOT the tool exit code), custom:rollback_executed_once (boolean; produced by the rollback-execution stage - executed, never merely documented), custom:fail_open_exit_zero_count_zero (boolean; produced by parsing the transport's own report for a zero-file count alongside a zero exit status; MUST be false). Producers cannot be written on the leaves: SEM-001 compares parse(source_expression) to the tree by dict equality and parse() emits no `producer` key - both-states probe at platform/council/_probe_note_vs_source_expression.py. The SEM-012 WARN is expected and non-blocking. || WHY THE THIRD CLAUSE IS A NOT: the fail-open shape is the one that passes both other clauses while deploying nothing. Encoding it as a positive requirement would let a silent zero-count run slip through as 'no evidence of failure'. Absence of evidence is not evidence here, so the rule asserts the failure shape is affirmatively absent.
